author: Jane Imbody
title: New Lexington FFA forestry team wins state title, advances to nationals - NewsBreak
text:
By Jane Imbody ,
19 hours ago New Lexington FFA members are headed to a national forestry competition after winning a state contest, adding to a fall that also included the chapter's annual canoe trip.
The chapter's forestry team took first place Sept. 26 at Hocking College in Nelsonville, according to a community announcement. The state championship qualifies the team to compete at the national competition in October 2027.
The Ohio FFA forestry career development event tested students on leaf identification, forest products and wood types, forestry equipment, topographic maps and a written exam. Students also completed a compass practicum involving azimuth readings and distances from designated points.
Andre Spicer finished first individually among almost 200 members. Chad Hatfield placed third, Arloine Metzger fourth, Marley Mendez-Santiago 11th, Drake Edwards 19th and Rebecca Gibbs 20th. Arleigh Gibson, Cambrie Murdock and Eilley Fink also were members of the team.
"Being a part of the forestry team really is an incredible experience," Spicer said. "From my freshman year to now, I have seen this team grow and improve, all with Mrs. Foster’s help. And this year, our team getting first in the state will be a truly unforgettable experience that I will miss so much."
The chapter plans to honor the team at the National FFA Convention next year, according to the announcement.
FFA canoe trip
Earlier in the month, New Lexington FFA members traded forestry competition for paddles during the chapter's annual canoe trip.
About 100 middle and high school students participated in the Sept. 15 event at Hocking Hills Canoe Livery in Logan. Members traveled five miles down the Hocking River while practicing communication, problem-solving, rowing and coordination skills.
Students navigated challenges that included paddling in sync and keeping their canoes dry. After completing the trip, members received food and drinks served by New Lexington FFA agriculture teachers.
"The canoe trip is always a super fun event that I look forward to every fall," New Lexington FFA member Eilley Fink said. "I got to bond with fellow members on a serene trip."
The chapter said the canoe trip is among the events it offers to encourage team bonding, personal growth and communication skills.
